plan.notes: Source: Official Western Washington University 2024-2025 catalog, Environmental Science, BS program page (catalog.wwu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=21&poid=10107; College of the Environment, Department of Environmental Sciences). The catalog specifies 109-110 credits: Preparatory Courses (44-45 cr.: BIOL 204/205/206, CHEM 161/162/163, MATH 124, PHYS 161, ENVS 203 or GEOL 211) and the Major (65 cr.: organic chemistry, ecology, biostatistics, CENV capstone, ESCI 498A/B/C/D, ENVS/UEPP 300/400 course, two lab/lecture options, and under-advisement electives). Because the live catalog page renders its Requirements table client-side, the requirement details were retrieved from an archived copy of this official catalog page; all courses, credits, and options are from the official 2024-2025 catalog. WWU is on the quarter system: the plan uses 12 quarters (Fall/Winter/Spring). The catalog's preparatory guidance (general chemistry freshman year, general biology sophomore year) sets the Year 1-2 order. University graduation requires 180 total credits including General University Requirements; GURs are modeled as constrained-choice slots (71 cr.) to complete the 180-credit degree plan. All credit values are quarter hours. No courses, credits, or prereqs invented.
